citations.title: Career outcomes of NIH career development (K) awardees
citations.what_it_says: Demonstrates that NIH K awardees are significantly more likely to obtain subsequent R01 funding than comparable non-K applicants, quantifying the K-to-R conversion advantage.

citations.authors: Jagsi R, DeCastro R, Griffith KA, et al.
citations.title: The Association of Mentored Research Career Development Awards with Subsequent Independent Research Funding
citations.what_it_says: Shows K23 and K08 awardees achieve R01 funding at roughly 2x the rate of unsuccessful K applicants and report stronger publication trajectories.

citations.authors: Goldstein MS, Scalzitti DA, et al.
citations.title: Outcomes of the NIH Career Development Awards for Physical Therapy Researchers
citations.what_it_says: Documents that PT K-awardees disproportionately become R-funded principal investigators and constitute a large share of NIH-funded rehab faculty.

citations.authors: NIH Advisory Committee to the Director
citations.title: Physician-Scientist Workforce Working Group Report
citations.what_it_says: Establishes K awards as the primary federal mechanism for transitioning mentored trainees to independent investigator status across clinical and rehab sciences.

citations.title: Predictors of Success in Obtaining an NIH R01 After a Mentored K Award
citations.what_it_says: Identifies publication productivity and mentor R-funding history during the K period as the strongest predictors of subsequent independent funding success.

citations.authors: Frontera WR, Bean JF, et al.
citations.title: Building the Rehabilitation Research Workforce: The Medical Rehabilitation Research Resource (MR3) and K12 Networks
citations.journal: American Journal of Physical Medicine & Rehabilitation
citations.what_it_says: Describes how K12 institutional programs have produced a generation of independently funded rehab scientists and underlie most NIH-funded rehab labs.

citations.title: NIH Data Book: Career Development Awards by Mechanism
citations.what_it_says: Reports K-series application success rates (~25-30%) and tracks subsequent R-series funding outcomes used to benchmark pathway-to-independence metrics.
